extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students of literature, psychoanalysis, and humor theory
extracted.subtask_description: A theoretical analysis of the technical means by which wit (word- and thought-wit) is produced, categorizing techniques (allusion, omission, comparison, condensation, displacement, etc.), their relations to dream-work, and the distinction between harmless and tendency-driven wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allusion through omission and contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Allusions effected by omission (and contradiction) are technical means of witticism: something omitted is replaced by an inference which 'strikes back as an allusion'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Heine's quips where omission implies an insulting reference; short conversational allusions (two Jews in front of bathing establishment). Note: omission can be 'filled in' by the hearer and become the witty thrust. Not every allusion is automatically witty — only those showing a 'witty' element count as wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allusion (indirect expression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allusion as a form of 'indirect expression' — a broad group including allusions, representation through the opposite, errors of thought, and unification—used to convey wit indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud suggests using 'indirect expression' as a comprehensive name to group various techniques (errors of thought—unification—indirect representation). Surrounding examples: many witticisms that rely on implication, inference, or symbolic substitution. Evaluate whether the indirectness itself produces the witty effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation through the minute (minute element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solving the problem by bringing the entire character to full expression through a minute or minutest detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the Jew who instantly changes behavior when asked about Yom Kippur (minute gesture reveals whole character); the physician who waits for labor cries before acting (change in cry reveals real state). Use trivial details that allow economy of expression and reveal larger trait/real situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison (simile/metaphor) as indirect expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of comparison to create witty impressions; comparisons often touch on different difficulties because it is sometimes unclear whether the wit comes from the comparison itself or from associated techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Lassalle's chemist analogy; Lichtenberg's 'torch of truth' — sometimes a comparison regains force by extension or deduction. Evaluate whether comparison alone produces wit or whether it relies on continuation, absurd attribute, unification, or restoration of a stale phrase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation / Unification of comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Extending a comparison into a sustained analogy or unification that links disparate elements under an 'unexpected association', creating wit by the surprise of the unification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: comparison of reviews to children's diseases continued to represent later fates of books; building on a comparison to deduce new aspects. This technique often belongs to 'unification' where the witty effect is in the associative leap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation through absurdity (absurd attributes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating baffling, absurd, or grotesque attributes by means of comparison or juxtaposition; the absurd attribute itself often carries the wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Lichtenberg's 'learned bowels' (absurd attribute revealed by comparison), 'bread-bread-glory' combinations. When a comparison yields an absurd attribute, the absurdity may be the true carrier of wit rather than the comparison's mere likeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peculiar (degrading) attributions / concrete-abstraction juxtaposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing abstractions beside very concrete or low things (a 'degrading' character) to produce a witty effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'pants of good-breeding', 'buttons tore from the pants of my patience'. Often produces a striking impression; consider speaker/context (e.g., clerk using trade metaphors) since appropriateness of voice can enhance the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manifold application of the same material (identical wit technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeatedly reusing the same material with peculiar modifications to produce a witty pattern or punning effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: playful rhymes and word switches (e.g., 'Lame Duck' pun). Technical name: 'Manifold Application of the Same Material'. Evaluate how variations on the same root material create cumulative wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literalizing or restoring the force of a degenerated phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking a blurred or fixed phrase in its full literal sense (or building further on it) to restore its original force and produce wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Lichtenberg's treatment of 'torch of truth' by extending the comparison to a deduction. This technique often interacts with identical-application or unification methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation with substitutive formation (nucleus of word-wit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensation combined with substitutive formation constitutes the nucleus of the technique of word-wit: overlapping meanings or compressed expression producing an economy of wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud relates this nucleus to the dream-work (condensation). Look for compressed expressions, double meanings, puns, and substitutive wordplay that economize verbal material to yield wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displacement (thought-wit mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of displacement (shifting emphasis or association) as a technique in thought-wit; parallels mechanisms found in dream-work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displacement creates unexpected associative targets and contributes to the strange or displaced appearance of wit. Evaluate whether shifting associations underlie the humorous effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation through the opposite
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressing something by stating or suggesting its opposite as a vehicle for wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed with other indirect-expression techniques; examine examples where saying the opposite yields an ironic or witty insight (contradiction-based effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy (tendency to economy) in wit
rubrics_metrics.description: A tendency to economy — concise, efficient expression — as a common final element in word-wit technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy often produces condensation and substitution that yield pleasure. Evaluate whether the joke's economy aids comprehension and punch; economy interacts with other techniques to heighten effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: Harmless (abstract) wit vs. Tendency-wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify wit as either 'harmless/abstract' (wit for its own sake, non-purposive) or 'tendency-wit' (wit serving a purpose or agenda).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmless wit is not necessarily shallow — it can be rich in content — and useful for theory because it isolates technique without purposive confounds. Tendency-wit has a purpose and therefore accesses pleasure sources unavailable to harmless wit; when evaluating wit, determine whether there is an underlying tendency or goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile wit (aggression, satire, defense)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subtype of tendency-wit where wit serves hostility: aggression, satire, or defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hostile wit risks ruffling the offended; technique may be identical to harmless wit but the purposive element can intensify the laugh effect. Evaluate intent, target, and potential for offense when producing or judging such wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obscene / Exhibitionary wit (sexual exhibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subtype of tendency-wit where wit serves the purpose of sexual exhibition or obscene display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically neglected but important: obscene wit uses similar techniques yet exploits sexual exhibition to access sources of pleasure distinct from harmless wit. Consider cultural norms and audience sensitivity when using/judging this tendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure (Lacheffekt) derived from technique
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of pleasure or laughableness arises from the technical operation of wit (condensation, displacement, indirect expression, etc.), not merely from content or purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freud's axiom: the mode of expression determines the character of wit. In evaluation, ask whether reducing the witty expression to plain sense removes the laugh effect — if so, the technique supplies the pleasure. Distinguish pleasure due to thought-content from pleasure due to technical word-play.
